sources.citation: Glottolog 5.2 languoid record ronj1237 (JSON) and OLAC combined catalogue page for roe (Internet Archive copy 2026-02-16)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are all 'a wordlist or less' (Carter 2012, Hooley 1971, Claassen & McElhanon 1970); OLAC lists only PARADISEC MR1-005 'Dangal Roinji Sio Mangga (wordlists)', Malcolm Ross 1980 audio, plus Glottolog and Ethnologue. No language description of Ronji exists in either catalogue.

sources.note: Nothing; free page now titled 'Uma Language (ROE)', summary only, details paywalled. Wikipedia 'Ronji language' page (read via direct download) has no phonology section either.

sources.citation: O'Bannon, Devin (SIL Global), with a supporting letter by Scot Stober dated 23 September 2024. 2025. ISO 639-3 Registration Authority Change Request 2025-039: Update language name [roe] Ronji to Uma; retain Ronji as additional name. Dallas: SIL International (status Pending, 2026-09-20).
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Pointer value: SIL-PNG (Stober, Mato programme) holds recent Uma literacy materials (8 primers, triglot picture dictionary, Genesis portion) and a 2020 unpublished survey ms; an orthography exists and an alphabet-design/OPD-type document may exist in the SIL-PNG archive, but none is online (Bloom Library 0 roe books; Webonary/pnglanguages 403). Also states Mato and Uma are 'only 54% similar'.

sources.citation: Carter, Jed, Beautlyn Eliab, Karl Kama, Roger Maikei, Devin O'Bannon & Napa Yanderave. 2023. Survey Report for Uma (Ronji) [roe], Tandɨ (Yagomi) [ygm], Muratayak [asx], Degenang (Degenan) [dge], and Forak [frq] Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2023-003. Dallas: SIL International. v+65 pp. (PDF 71 pp; ISSN 2766-9327).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing. For Uma the 2020 survey assessed vitality only (EGIDS 6b); wordlists were transcribed only in Yagomi, Seure, Sel, Mamgak and Faigurup, so the report has no Uma language data beyond population, language-use and attitude responses. stress/tone/accent/syllable/phonology do not occur (one hit = gloss 'stone'). Sec. 1.2.1 lists unpublished SIL-PNG Ronji items not in Glottolog or our bibliography: McHenry, Stober & Troolin 1996; Stober 1996 wordlists (Roinji, Gali); Stober 2009 visit report; SIL-PNG n.d. English-Kate survey list Roinji.

sources.citation: Stober, Scot (compiler), with the Mato and Uma language communities. 2020. Mato Dictionary: Mato - English - Tok Pisin - Uma. Webonary.org. Dallas: SIL International. (c) 2020 SIL International. Online dictionary with 'Browse Uma' reversal index (3 pages) and Language > Phonology / Grammar pages; read in the Internet Archive capture of 26 Feb 2025.
sources.note: For Uma/Ronji: wordlist-only data - an alphabetical index of Uma headwords in a practical orthography (letters a b d e g i j k l m n ng o p r s t u w x y; e.g. abura, aloxaya, amboga boronga, amtum, ananasi) keyed to Mato entries, with no stress or tone marks and no statement about Uma sound structure anywhere on the captured pages. The site's Phonology page is about Mato [met] and reads 'Stress is predictable and usually falls on the penultimate syllable. Exceptions occur when heavy syllables attract word-final stress.' (referring to the Mato Organized Phonology Data 2005) - this is ANOTHER…

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J., Robert Blust & Russell D. Gray (eds). 2008-. Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database, language no. 1348 'Roinji'. Source: Lincoln, Piet (n.d.) 'Rai Coast Survey' [= Lincoln 1976e, Rai Coast Austronesian language survey data, mimeo]; typed/checked by Kwang-Ju Cho. 191 of 210 items. (Greenhill, Blust & Gray 2008, Evolutionary Bioinformatics 4: 271-283.) CC BY 4.0.
sources.note: Nothing. Lincoln's Roinji forms as entered in ABVD are segmental transcriptions (character set a b d e g h i k l m n o p r s t u w y z ŋ ɛ ɡ ɣ β, morpheme hyphens, '~' for variants); a scripted scan of all 191 items finds no stress mark (ˈ ˌ ' acute/grave), no length mark and no tone notation, and the language page has no phonological notes field content. Wordlist-level evidence only; whether Lincoln's original mimeo sheets marked stress cannot be told from the ABVD entry.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 2007. Calquing and metatypy. Journal of Language Contact THEMA 1: 116-143. DOI 10.1163/000000007792548341. (Open copy: ANU Open Research hdl 1885/19809.)
sources.note: Nothing about Ronji prosody. Gives first-hand Ronji clause data (ex. 1b 'ŋa to ŋa-ɣaŋ saula' IRR S:1s-eat banana 'I shall eat banana'; ɣaŋ 'eat', ŋa 'I', ŋa- s:1s) and typological facts (SVO, no determiner, preverbal irrealis) as the non-metatypised comparison for Takia; 'pitch accent'/'intonation' occur only re Yiddish and Takia focus. Descriptive beyond a wordlist, silent on stress/tone. Pointer: Ross holds Ronji grammatical fieldnotes beyond the PARADISEC MR1-005 tape.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University. (hdl 1885/146624)
sources.note: Not a description; establishes the (empty) state of Roinji documentation to 1995 and the citable form of Lincoln's report. McElhanon 1978 ('A classification of the languages of the Morobe Province', mimeo/UPNG) is the one indexed item neither Glottolog nor our bibliography lists; it is a classification, not a description.

sources.note: Nothing. Roinji appears once, in the Ngero-Vitiaz subgrouping tree. ANU Open Research hdl 1885/253752.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing for Roinji. Roinji data (informant Kelu Tokno of Roinji village; written source Lincoln 1976e) occur only in Ngero/Vitiaz sound-correspondence tables and reflex lists (index: pp. 48-49, 64, 70, 84, 115, 419). 'Stress' occurs in the book only in the Schouten (Ali/Tumleo) Verner's-law discussion and general remarks. Silent on Roinji stress.

sources.citation: Smith, Geoffrey P. 1988. Morobe counting systems. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 1-132. Canberra: Australian National University. (hdl 1885/253560)
sources.note: No phonology content: numeral forms in plain orthography without stress marks; the only occurrences of 'stress(ed)' in the volume are the ordinary English verb. Useful only as a further citation of Lincoln (1976) as a Roinji data source.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1986. Refugees, traders, and other wanderers: the linguistic effects of population mixing in Melanesia. In P. Geraghty, L. Carrington & S. A. Wurm (eds), FOCAL II (Pacific Linguistics C-94), 407-434.
sources.note: Nothing; one geographic mention ('on the Rai Coast of New Guinea from Kaiwa to Roinji'). downloaded from the ANU search hit for 'Mur village'; kept for the record.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1986. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. PhD thesis, Australian National University. xvi+514 leaves. (hdl 1885/133651; thesis version of Ross 1988, PL C-98)
sources.note: Segmental historical phonology only: Roinji appears 47 times, always as reflexes in sound-correspondence sets (e.g. Roinji piso(a)-, kuya, suvi-, pana-zi) plus the remark that POc *t lenition is phonemic in Roinji. The word 'stress' occurs only in the table conventions ('Occasionally the environment is an unstressed (as opposed to a stressed) syllable.. indicated by an upper-case superscript U') and in a Markham-family passage; no environment of that kind is invoked for Roinji and nothing is said about where Roinji stress falls or about tone.

sources.citation: Hooley, Bruce A. 1971. Austronesian Languages of the Morobe District, Papua New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 10(2): 79-151.
sources.note: Glottolog's second-ranked source (wordlist type); contains the Roinji wordlist used for lexicostatistics and possibly a note on transcription conventions. Low chance of a stress statement.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11 (Pacific Linguistics A-23), 45-78. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing for Roinji. Sec. 5.1 (p.62) only says 'The Roinji language is spoken in the villages of Roinji and Gali near the mouth of the Yupna River'; fn.7 gives 27% shared vocabulary with Gedaged. The typological section 6.1 Phonology compares one Papuan language per family (Saep, Suroi, Kolom, Sinsauru, Rawa, Kewieng, Uruwa, Wantoat, Uri); its only stress sentence (p.~66) is 'Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat' - Papuan languages, not Roinji. ANU Open Research hdl 1885/254286.
